title: Frontend: usePreviousHook
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind usePreviousHook. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({initial=0}). Implement usePrevious with a ref updated after commit. Show current in [data-testid="current"] and previous committed value in [data-testid="previous"], initially none. Increment updates current; unrelated renders are excluded from this bounded contract.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use a ref to retain the prior value and update it in an effect after commit.
alternativeApproaches: Implement previous-distinct-value semantics and explain how it differs from previous-render semantics.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: First render; changed value; unchanged value.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
